- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Forecast tends to lag by 1–3 days in upward trends; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5 units to early forecast values if sentiment is rising.  
- After a strong price spike (forecast > 65), model often overcorrects downward; cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast is erratic, apply smoothing: average last 3–5 forecast values before final output.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 60–65, adjust forecast mean downward by 2–5 units if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
